correctness.rationale: The x-first and y-first matrices were explicitly derived. Both preserve strictly positive definite quadratic forms for 0<t<2. Their fair average squared-norm pullback equals (1+t^4/2)I, proving the exact all-n recursion. The full bias covariance transfer determinant at eigenvalue 1 equals -8p(1-p)t^6, so a real root exceeds one. A positive Perron eigenmatrix for the adjoint map is PD because the elliptic x-first matrix has no real invariant line, yielding an exponential lower bound for every nonzero initial state. Native symbolic/rational checker passed 136 assertions; infinite conclusions are analytical.

value.rationale: The question whether randomizing an order of two individually elliptic, power-bounded bilinear optimization sweeps preserves the important stability property is natural, distinct from simultaneous gradient descent, and algorithmically consequential. The theorem identifies a sharp zero/random-switching frontier for every normalized step in (0,2) and gives the exact mean-square growth factor for unbiased choice. Its finite-dimensional certificate and explicitly delimited assumptions make it a reproducible benchmark.
